title: The inward eye
hookLine: a walk by a lake, a sister's journal, and daffodils that flash upon the inward eye (I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud)
tomorrow: a poet says we gave our hearts away. for what?

cards: Camera rolls fill up with sunsets nobody looks at twice. William Wordsworth had no camera. He had a sister with a notebook.
Dorothy Wordsworth wrote in her journal about a windy walk the two of them took by a lake, where daffodils ran along the shore, tossing, as she described them, as if they were laughing with the wind.
Later William turned that walk into a poem. And the moment it builds to doesn't happen at the lake at all. It happens on a couch, with his eyes shut.

teach.h: THEY FLASH UPON THAT INWARD EYE.
teach.b: Here it is: "For oft, when on my couch I lie / In vacant or in pensive mood, / They flash upon that inward eye / Which is the bliss of solitude; / And then my heart with pleasure fills, / And dances with the daffodils."
The inward eye is memory, but more than storage. It's a scene taken in once, kept, and given back when you're still. Notice one thing the poem changes.

It says I wandered lonely as a cloud, but the journal says there were two of them, walking together in the wind. The poem lets the walker be alone, because it is about what solitude does with a scene.
Wordsworth named the idea in his preface to Lyrical Ballads, where he wrote that poetry "takes its origin from emotion recollected in tranquillity."

teach.h: THE SENSES TAKE IT IN; STILLNESS GIVES BACK.
teach.b: That's the Romantic teaching under the poem: the world comes in through the senses, and the quiet mind turns it into something that feeds you later.

teach.h: MARY WROTE THE BEST TWO LINES.
teach.b: One to tell a friend tonight: Wordsworth said the two best lines in the poem were by his wife, Mary.
Tradition says they're the inward eye lines. So the poem had three makers: Dorothy's notebook, William's verse, Mary's two lines.

how: Readers of I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud turn to Dorothy Wordsworth's Grasmere journal for the walk behind the poem.

o: the conscience that watches over all that you do
the mind's eye that sees a scene again in stillness
a hidden third eye that is able to see the future

games.q: on a hike, a friend says she can only enjoy the view if she photographs all of it. what fits Wordsworth's inward eye?
o: look long enough to take it in; the still mind can give it back later.
photograph everything; memory fades, so pictures are the only way to keep it.
never think about it afterward; looking back always spoils a good day.
games.why: the daffodils come back to Wordsworth on his couch, emotion recollected in tranquillity. the looking is what the inward eye keeps.

practice: Close your eyes and bring back one bright scene you've lived: a field, a face, a kitchen light at night. Let it flash on the inward eye and stay with it for two minutes, the colors, the air, who was there.
If your heart fills, let it.

wordCard.voice: The inward eye: Wordsworth's name for the mind seeing a scene again, in stillness. And the line that names it may be Mary's.

carryVoice: Your line: the inward eye, where the daffodils keep dancing. One week of poets, gathered in.
